Max: FYI - I am seeing a 2.3x p99 regression on Mixtral-8x when paged-KV is enabled and RoPE scaling is on. Baseline (no paged-kv): p99=38ms, with paged-kv+RoPE-scale: p99=87ms for generate(512).
Sam: repro steps? quick numbers?
Max: Ran local bench on a single A100, command: `runtest --model mixtral-8x --kv-layout paged --rope-scale 1.5 --seq 512 --batch 1 --warm 50 --iters 200`.
Devon: can you paste perf profile output (flame/ops breakdown)?
Max: pasted profiler snippet:
```
[profiling] total_tokens: 102400
- attention_kernel_misaligned: 42.1% (wall 4923ms)
- kv_read_page: 28.7% (wall 3358ms)
- continuous_batching: 9.4% (wall 1100ms)
- cuda_memcpy: 6.5% (wall 760ms)
- other (compute): 13.3% (wall 1550ms)
```
Max: runtime kernel selection log shows repeated fallback entries:
```
kernel_selector: requested head_size=64, kv_dim=64 -> no optimized kernel for (64,64) alignments, falling back to generic_gemm
kernel_selector: optimized kernels exist for head_size={32,128} only
```
Anya: that's telling. The paged layout allocates KV in 128-slot pages and our head_size=64 leads to half-page slop and extra page reads + fragmentation. RoPE scaling increased effective seq length distribution -> more pages touched per request.
Lina: I saw a similar pattern on Qwen where num_key_value_heads mismatch caused double page reads. Did you check num_key_value_heads for this model? 
Max: mixtral config: `num_key_value_heads=32`, `head_dim=64`, `kv_page_slots=128`, page_granularity=128.
Sam: so two issues: (1) kernel_selector has no optimized kernel for 64x64 -> triggers slower generic kernel; (2) paged allocator hits extra pages because head/chunk packing is suboptimal.
Devon: quick microbench: I ran matrix-mul kernels with head_dim 64 on prod-driver vs patch. Results:
- generic_gemm: 1.0x baseline (slow)
- tuned_aligned_kernel (patched to handle 64): 0.58x (faster)
Command: `./bench_kernel --m 512 --n 64 --k 1024 --dtype fp16`
Sam: is there a simple runtime patch: prefer 128-pair kernel when head_dim==64 by fusing two heads? That might reduce kernel fallback but increases register pressure.
Anya: other option: adjust paged allocator to use 64-slot subpages when model head dim=64 and num_heads%2==0 -> reduces page fragmentation. That avoids extra device reads at the cost of more metadata.
Max: I ran the patched allocator (compact-kv-v2) locally: p99 dropped from 87ms -> 51ms, flame shows attention_kernel_misaligned down to 18% and kv_read_page down to 12%.
Infra Bot: deploy-check: canary group for runtime-patch exists: runtime-canary-2026-03 (10% traffic) - no regressions in basic smoke.
Lina: nice. Any accuracy/quality impacts from the kernel change (reordering/fusion)?
Devon: kernel change is purely compute layout; we validated logits for 100 random prompts vs reference -> bit-exact for fp16 path where expected, and max L2 diff < 1e-3 for quant path.
Sam: plan suggestion:
1) revert paged-kv default for mixtral-family on current prod (rollback flag) to stop regression ASAP.
2) land compact-kv-v2 as opt-in behind model flags; run fleet canary.
3) upstream kernel_selector: add 64x64 optimized kernel or a fused two-headed kernel fallback.
4) add bench harness for page-fragmentation (per-model) and automated perf alerts when p99 increases >20%.
Max: I created a perf issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-8723 (notes + profiler + microbench). Linking patch branches there.
Anya: I'll own allocator opt-in rollout. Sam: can you take kernel_selector change? Devon: help with microbench and CI perf jobs.
Lina: I'll add an eval to ensure no output-quality drift for models affected.
Max: thanks all. Leaving logs & full profile in the issue. Quick follow-up: can someone run `bench_kv_frag --model mixtral-8x --heads 32 --head-dim 64 --pages 128 --rope-scale 1.5` across a small cluster and paste raw numbers here?
Sam: on it, will post results in thread by EOD.
Infra Bot: note: created perf-sla-alert INF-8723-canary and scheduled 24h watch.
